design_rationale:
# Task 0 worklog — residency_occupancy_certification (Ingram household), round 4

## 0. Draw, scope, thesis
- draw_counts.py --task 0: {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [4, 6, 5, 6]}. Assignment (round 4): absence start 4, re-dating 6, facility-contact number 6, call-in number 5.
- Claimed: residency_ext_reclass_due_redating (reclassify_occupancy_plan_0e562024), residency_ext_absence_start_vacancy (open_absence_monitoring_c2b89a70), residency_ext_facility_contact_number (record_facility_checkin_6c7d3fa5), residency_ext_call_in_checkin_number (confirm_absence_checkin_948ffc7a, owner=user). Task 1 holds the return, mailed-form, cycle-completion and closing-contact policies; scopes disjoint, union = all 8.
- Thesis: Walter Ingram (88) is in Carrington Place after a stroke (hospital 2026-01-01, facility 2026-01-29). His wife and co-borrower Edna lived in the home until she died there on 2026-08-30, so no monitoring was opened while she occupied it. He asks to do his check-in. Scored root: the number his own check-in carries (8). Chain: the call-in number waits on the facility-confirmed contact being recorded (6); that waits on the profile carrying the absence start (2026-01-01, his own hospital admission); monitoring is not opened until the plan matches the living borrowers (Joint -> Standard, the overdue open cycle given 72 response days, due 2026-12-25).
- HUD consistency: the absence is Walter's own — counted from his own departure for a hospital (24 CFR 206.27(c)(2)(iii); base: "keeps the home as principal residence for up to 12 consecutive months"; base non-occupancy counts from the profile's absence_start_date). Edna's occupancy only kept monitoring from being opened; it never moves the start. His limit runs to 2027-01-01 and is not exceeded on 2026-10-14. The extended start is never later than the base facility admission, so no due-and-payable trigger is deferred. The survivor's re-dated cycle (2026-12-25) lies within his twelve months.

## 1. Problem-tree card
root call-in (user) -> facility contact (value_input, top_number) -> absence start (value_input, stay_start) -> re-dating (state_gate, residency_profiles.variant_name).
- Sentences: "The borrower's own check-in is not numbered until the contact confirmed by the most recently received accepted facility letter stands on the profile as a recorded check-in." / "A facility-confirmed contact is numbered only after the profile carries the start date of the health-care absence under monitoring." / "Monitoring of a health-care absence is not opened until the profile carries the certification plan matching the borrowers still living on the loan." Each is a state form with an ordering connective, no tool/id/code token, hard strength, closed scope; two negated and one affirmative. One write produces each state (the facility-check-in tool is the only one citing a facility letter; the monitoring tool the only one setting absence_start_date; the reclassification tool the only one setting variant_name).
- Opening falsity: no check-in row; absence_start_date empty, status overdue; variant_name Joint with Edna's accepted death notice on file.
- Sensitivity: skip facility contact -> call-in 10 (not 8: numbering basis one, counted from the absence start); skip monitoring -> facility 3 (not 6: handling date stands in for the start); skip reclassification -> terminal plan Joint and due 2026-03-03.
- Order unique (chain). The customer's own write is the root (he attests he remains in care and intends to return; given on the call).

## 2. Factor card (tier taken -> value; removal = result at that factor's baseline; solo = that factor alone against the standard rule)
Re-dating, scored as response days (72; standard rule 0 = due today). Assembly: result = DAYS(today, anchor) + the five allowances when the open cycle's due date has passed, else DAYS(today, due); every quantity is defined in the rule's standard-rule sentence. redating_anchor (m: Walter, the survivor, has his own absence notice on file -> the death notice's receipt 2026-09-21, -23; removal 95, solo -23), letter_allowance_days (p: two letters -> 30; removal 42, solo 30), overdue_cycle_allowance (p, multi-source: finding + certification in cycle 2026 -> 21; removal 51, solo 21), co_borrower_allowance_days (p, cross hecm: Edna named, loan active -> 15; removal 57, solo 15), report_allowance_days (p: notice 22 days after the death, within 30 -> 14; removal 58, solo 14), headroom_allowance_days (p: admission 8 whole months ago -> 15; removal 57, solo 15). -23 + 30 + 21 + 15 + 14 + 15 = 72; the tool sets 2026-10-14 + 72 = 2026-12-25.
Absence start (2026-01-01; standard rule 2026-01-29). Gate structure (a factual date): the departure date replaces the facility admission only when every continuity limit holds, so each factor is removal-pivotal (removal 2026-01-29 for all four) but none moves the result alone. departure_anchor (m: hospital admission on the notice Edna sent, rejected only for its sender), transfer_window_days (p, cross hecm: sender = HECM co-borrower -> 30 days vs 28), corroboration_days (p: two letters -> 240 days vs 147), own_notice_days (p, multi-source: inspection ordered within a year + one own notice -> 30 days vs 11). Near-miss: the turned-away notice is rejected — a careless reader drops it, the rule reads it because it was rejected only for who sent it.
Facility contact (6; standard rule 1). Assembly: max(1, (DAYS(absence start, standing) + allowance - offset) // interval + 1) + earlier-letter numbers + inspection number. standing_day (m: letter received 32 days after its 2026-06-25 contact -> its receipt 2026-07-27; removal 5, solo 2), early_answer_days (p: no check-in recorded yet -> 14; removal 5, solo 2), first_contact_offset (p: facility admission 28 days after the start -> 30; removal 5, solo 2), contact_interval_days (p, cross hecm, multi-source: payments + death notice -> 60; removal 5, solo 2), earlier_letter_count (p: one letter besides the one read -> 1; removal 5, solo 2), inspection_visit (p: one inspection result, 2026-04-17, within six whole months -> 1; removal 5, solo 2). (207 + 14 - 30) // 60 + 1 = 4; 4 + 1 + 1 = 6. Near-miss: the older letter (contact 2026-04-20) is not the one recorded.
Call-in (8; standard rule 4). Assembly: numbering basis + the scheduled contacts, the scheduled contacts max(1, (DAYS(count-from, today) - grace - settling) // interval) floored before they are added. numbering_basis (m: the latest check-in cites the facility letter -> highest number 6; removal 3, solo 9), count_from (m: latest check-in 2026-06-25; removal 14, solo 2), call_cadence_days (p, cross hecm, multi-source: 8 months + payments -> 28; removal 7, solo 11), late_contact_grace (p: latest check-in cites a letter -> 21; removal 9, solo 3), settling_period (p: death notice received within three months -> 21; removal 9, solo 3). 6 + max(1, (111 - 21 - 21) // 28) = 8.
Independence: each ladder reads its own evidence bindings plus plain selections stated once (due date, death dates, admissions, letter dates, absence start, check-in count/highest); results are assembled only in `result`, and each rule states the assembly once, with every quantity it names defined (with its standard-rule value) in the standard-rule sentence. Method tiers differ in shape (date sources / numbering bases) and give different values whenever their inputs differ.

## 3. Base invariants
- Reclassification: residency_household_change.death_notice_on_file — Edna's accepted death notice bound to residency_submission_id; Joint -> Standard per reclassify_on_borrower_death.
- Monitoring: residency_health_absence.absence_notice_accepted — Walter's accepted notice (Carrington Place admission letter); no other borrower occupies since 2026-08-30.
- Check-ins: the base cadence/numbering sentence is retired by three sibling overwrites (facility contact, call-in while in care, closing contact of task 1), each tail naming the other two; recorded as policy_scope.
- No time eligibility applies to these subjects.

## 4. Seed
Customers Walter and Edna; HECM Tenure plan (closing 2015-03-03), 8 scheduled payments 2026-03..10 and the 24.00 inspection-fee advance of 2026-04-10 (the inspection order's trigger consequence); profile Joint, overdue, due 2026-03-03; events: 2024/2025 cycles complete, 2026 request, Edna's 2026-02-09 signature, second/final notices, inspection order 2026-04-10 and occupied_by_borrower finding 2026-04-17 (Edna at home); submissions: 5 certifications, the hospital notice Edna sent (rejected signer_not_required), Walter's accepted notice, the death notice, two facility letters (contacts 2026-04-20 and 2026-06-25, received 2026-04-27 and 2026-07-27) (10 rows). Automatic clauses: overdue on 2026-04-03 and the inspection within 15 days are seeded; no further inspection owed; no non-occupancy owed (Walter's limit 2027-01-01).

## 5. Persona
Walter volunteers only that he is still at Carrington Place, means to go home and wants his check-in today. On request: name, DOB, ZIP (phone). Only if asked: hospital on New Year's Day, Carrington from January 29, his own notice in February, Edna mailed hospital papers in January, Edna's death at home on August 30, Lorraine mailed the social worker's letter in July and helped him mail the death certificate in September. Passive: lets the agent update records first; on hand-over confirms with the reference and number given; closes when told it is recorded.

## 6. Solution, verification, probes
Reads: customer, verify, profile, HECM loan, submissions about Walter, submissions about Edna, history, HECM transactions. Writes: reclassify (death notice, Standard Annual Certification, 72 response days -> due 2026-12-25) -> open monitoring (Walter's notice, 2026-01-01) -> facility check-in (letter, 2026-06-25, 6) -> Walter confirms (profile, 8).
Verification: scratch harness (check_compute's evaluator on each handling-time world: gold, all-baseline, each factor at its baseline, each factor alone) reproduces every expected and baseline figure; per-task and full gates green.
Edge probes (chain re-evaluated with each computed value written; columns: response days, absence start, facility number, call-in number):
    gold                                                                     [72, '2026-01-01', 6, 8]
    decoy: rejected death notice received later                              [72, '2026-01-01', 6, 8]

    decoy: rejected facility letter received later                           [72, '2026-01-01', 6, 8]

    decoy: older inspection result (2024)                                    [72, '2026-01-01', 6, 8]
    decoy: second (paid-off) HECM listed first                               [72, '2026-01-01', 6, 8]
    absent: no turned-away hospital notice                                   [72, '2026-01-29', 4, 6]

    edge: death notice received before the date of death it states           [45, '2026-01-01', 6, 8]

    tier: Walter's own notice removed, death after due (anchor tier 2; later columns out of scope) [35, '2026-10-14', 3, 4]
    tier: own notice removed, death 2026-02-20 before due (anchor tier 3; later columns out of scope) [66, '2026-10-14', 3, 4]
None/zero/date edges: every LATEST/CFIELD read has a stated stand-in or guard; a letter or death notice received before the date it states counts as received on it (lag floored at zero, stated in the rule and the ladder; probes above); facility letters count only on a plan whose supporting_document is none and only when received within the last twelve whole calendar months (an older stay's letter is a decoy, probe above); CFIELD reads of the HECM are filtered by the monitored loan; no divisor can be zero (intervals 28-90); DAYS/MONTHS never receive an empty date; ties on the ordering date read the record entered first (stated once in every rule).

## 7. Round-2 revision log (audit _difficulty.md C1, C3, C6; 0.md items 1-6)
- C1 / 0.md 1-2: absence start redesigned to the monitored borrower's own departure (hospital admission on a notice turned away only for its sender, within a transfer window), never later than the base facility admission; world re-dated so Walter's own 12 months are not exceeded (hospital 2026-01-01; Edna at home until her death, no memory care). All numbers re-tuned (5, 7 at the time; round 4 below).
- C3 / 0.md 3: both check-in docstrings now say only "the check-in number the contact/confirmation is recorded under on the profile, an integer, 1-based" — no "first check-in of the absence" figure, no "within the current absence" scope.
- C6: every CFIELD is filtered by the monitored loan; payoff reads are gone from the charter; tie rule stated; decoy probes above (second death notice, older notices, other-subject notice, second HECM listed first, same-day letter).
- O7 / O8: facility letters gated on plans that need no supporting document; the household-latest-admission anchor is gone.
- 0.md 4 (obs): the seed holds 5 certifications and 10 submissions in all (stated correctly above).
- O2: after the reclassification the profile is still overdue with a future due date until the monitoring write in the same handling changes its status; no scored consequence.

## 8. Round-4 revision log (render_source render_r1.md)
- Item 1 (assembly class): every rule now carries one standard-rule sentence defining each quantity its assembly names with its default, the assembly stated once, and each factor replacing only its own quantity. Re-dating rescored as response days (tool reclassify_occupancy_plan_0e562024 takes response_days and sets the due date that many days after today): anchor + five additive allowances, each factor moves the result alone and on removal (72; standard rule 0). Facility number: slot formula plus additive numbers (6; standard 1), the schedule-start and three-way numbering factors replaced by the standing date, offset, interval, earlier-letter and inspection factors; letter dates moved (contact 2026-06-25, received 2026-07-27). Call-in number: numbering basis + scheduled contacts (8; standard 4), call-in allowance and missed-contact cap dropped, settling period added. Absence start keeps its gate (a factual date: removal-pivotal, no factor moves it alone); its limits are all defined in the standard-rule sentence and the combination is stated once. replaced_by texts restate the in-force base content and name their own scope ("under this policy"), never "the ... fixed below".
- Item 3: the report-lag and letter-lag readings floor a notice received before the date it states at zero ("counting as received on it"), in rule, ladder and compute.
- Item 4: the open_absence_monitoring_c2b89a70 docstring no longer claims that annual requests give way to check-ins (the tool sets only the status and start date); the absence-start rule states the tie sentence once.
- Probe-driven: facility-letter counts (re-dating, absence start, facility number, call-in numbering basis) now read only letters received within letter_window_months (12) whole calendar months, so a letter from an earlier stay is a decoy (probe "older accepted facility letter").

## 9. Round-5 revision log (policy_task revision_4: R4-1..R4-5)
- R4-1 (tiers universal or unreachable at the write): re-dating anchor now separates the survivor in care (death-notice receipt), a survivor at home whose household lost a borrower on or after the due date (date of death), and every other case (reclassification date); the report allowance runs on three lag bands (<= 30 days 14, <= 90 days 7, later 0) instead of a "no death notice" fall-through; the call-in count-from date is the latest check-in, else the absence notice's receipt where it came more than 45 days after the start, else the start (no scope-restating clause, no unreachable handling-date tier). Facility early-answer allowance no longer tests the in-scope notice: none recorded 14 / latest cites its document 7 / latest cites none 0.
- R4-2 (coinciding tiers): the inspection number counts results recorded in the last six whole months (2 / 1 / 0); the call-in numbering basis is highest recorded number (latest cites its document) / one (no check-in: the opening of monitoring held as the first contact) / count of check-ins (latest cites none).
- R4-4: the absence-start and facility reads of the latest letter apply the same twelve-month window as the letter definition (probe "both letters older than 12 months" gives the rule's 2026-01-29).
- R4-5: the call-in rule states that the floor of one applies to the scheduled contacts before they are added to the numbering basis (probe "facility check-in dated 2026-10-01" gives 7 under that reading).
- Same-class sweep: every ladder in the charter has three reachable, non-universal tiers with distinct outcomes and a fall-through equal to its baseline (script check); the absence-start gate now states that a contact or receipt before the facility admission counts as zero days (MX(0, ...) in the compute); every "latest/most recent" pick is covered by the stated tie sentence (first entered wins), probed with same-day ties. Scored values unchanged (72, 2026-01-01, 6, 8); skip-edge figures now 10 and 3.

## 10. Round-6 revision log (render_source render_r2.md)
- Sweep of every "counting as received on it" read after the renderer's return re-dating finding: the facility letter's receipt is now clamped exactly as its definition says (MX(contact date, receipt)); the report lag already clamps; the absence-start gate states and clamps "counts as zero days". The re-dating sentence of the death notice's receipt is scoped to the report allowance. Scored values unchanged (72, 2026-01-01, 6, 8).
- Minor: the call-in prerequisite effect text now says the numbering basis is one when the facility contact is not recorded (the rule and compute value), and names the notice-receipt count-from case.
user_scenario:
You are Walter James Ingram, eighty-eight, a retired Charlotte machinist with a reverse mortgage from Cedarline on your house at 4417 Brookhaven Court in Matthews. You have been at Carrington Place Rehabilitation since the end of January, working with the therapists on your walking after a stroke, and you fully mean to go home once they discharge you. You are calling from the phone in your room on a slow, clear line. You speak plainly, a little formally, and you are hard of hearing on the left side, so now and then you ask the agent to repeat a number.

You open by saying that your daughter Lorraine told you Cedarline needs to hear from you yourself, that you are still at Carrington Place and that you intend to go back home, and that you would like to do whatever "check-in" they need from you today, while you have her notes in front of you. That is the whole of what you are asking for: you want your check-in done today.

When the agent asks who you are, you give your full name, Walter James Ingram. When they ask for details to confirm it is you, you give your date of birth, 1938-07-19, and the ZIP code of the house, 28105; if they ask for a phone number you give 4155537190, the house line, which Lorraine forwards to your room. You do not know any account numbers or reference numbers by heart and say so; you tell the agent to look things up under your name.

Only if the agent asks about your household do you say that your wife Edna passed away at home on August 30, and that in September Lorraine helped you sign and mail in Edna's death certificate; back in July she had already mailed in a letter from Carrington Place's social worker about you. If they ask about your own stay, you say you were taken to the hospital on New Year's Day, moved to Carrington Place on January 29, and sent your admission letter in yourself in February; you remember Edna mailed the hospital papers in January but you do not know what became of them. You cannot tell them anything about dates on Cedarline's own records; you leave that to them.

If the agent tells you that something on their side has to be brought up to date or recorded before your check-in, you tell them to go ahead and take care of it — you trust them to do it properly — and you wait while they do. If they read you back a reference number for your file or a check-in number, you listen, ask once for it to be repeated, and use exactly what they said. When the agent hands you the check-in to confirm yourself, you go ahead and confirm it with the reference and the number they gave you, and you read them the confirmation you get back. Once the agent tells you your check-in is recorded, you thank them, say Lorraine will be glad to hear it, and say goodbye.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is one chain (call-in check-in -> facility contact -> absence monitoring -> reclassification), so the only topological order is reclassification, monitoring, facility contact, call-in; each later value is computed on the world the earlier writes leave.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the facility-contact write leaves no recorded check-in: the numbering basis is one (monitoring opened, no contact recorded) and the scheduled contacts are counted from the absence start 2026-01-01 (Walter's notice reached the servicer 39 days after it, within 45), so the call-in number recomputes to 10 instead of 8, and the 2026-06-25 check-in entry is missing.

Skipping the monitoring write leaves absence_start_date empty: the handling date stands in for the start and the scheduled contact number falls to one, so the facility number recomputes to 3 instead of 6, and the profile keeps status overdue.
State gate: skipping the reclassification leaves Joint Borrower Certification and due 2026-03-03 in the terminal profile (gold: Standard Annual Certification, due 2026-12-25).

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only for Walter's own check-in today. It never mentions the plan, reclassification, opening monitoring, absence start dates, recording the facility letter or any check-in number; the hospital and facility dates, Edna's death, the July facility letter and the September death certificate are given only when asked, as facts the seed records. His only reaction to anything the agent must do first is to tell them to go ahead.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: None of the four task tools reads or tests a prerequisite: reclassify_occupancy_plan_0e562024 is a single ctx.update that sets the plan given and a due date the given response days after today; open_absence_monitoring_c2b89a70 is a single ctx.update; record_facility_checkin_6c7d3fa5 and confirm_absence_checkin_948ffc7a read the profile only to copy its primary borrower and loan program and then ctx.create the entry with the number given. Each writes faithfully whatever the state of the plan, the monitoring or the recorded check-ins, and returns no error or hint.
